title: A second unpaired absence assertion: the --across-refs absent-row pairs its positive against a different list (found by QCLI-298)
description:
Found by QCLI-298's enumeration of absence-shaped assertions across test/, which the filing scoped to one row (the --ready row in test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts). This is a SECOND unpaired row of the same class in the collection-subject domain, recorded as a candidate there and not fixed there (out of AC1 scope).

DEFECT: test/qcli417-across-refs.test.ts:782 asserts expect(envelope.data.map((row) => row.id)).not.toContain(id) -- that a record created only UNCOMMITTED is absent from the `task list --across-refs` view. The only positive in that test is over `local.data` (a plain `task list`, a DIFFERENT source): expect(local.data.map((row) => row.id)).toContain(id). Nothing establishes that `envelope.data` -- the across-refs list the absence claim is actually about -- is populated, so an EMPTY across-refs view satisfies the row vacuously while proving nothing about the working-tree-versus-view distinction the test exists to prove. Under QCLI-298's classification rule (a positive pairs the check iff it establishes the POPULATION precondition over the SAME SUBJECT and the SAME SOURCE), this row is unpaired.

REPAIR: assert a known-present id IS in the across-refs list (over the same list and source) before asserting the created id is absent, and show the hardening fails on a deliberately emptied across-refs list -- the same self-sufficiency property QCLI-298 restored for the --ready row.

Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction context (QCLI-298 landed 2026-10-11).

acceptanceCriteria.text: test/qcli417-across-refs.test.ts:782 asserts a known-present id IS present in the across-refs list, over the same list and the same source, before asserting the id created only uncommitted is absent
The repair is shown to fail on purpose: with the presence assertion in place, a deliberately emptied across-refs list turns the row red
